[LDET.1.12] **Settings never change a result.** A program's capability
settings ([LCAP.1]) may restrict which constructs it may use and choose how
the engine executes it. They must not change what it computes. For one
source, one event trace and one platform, any two settings under which the
source compiles produce the same observable output, provided neither run
meets a capacity fault or a deadline halt.

The capacity fault and the deadline halt are the residue ([STYL.2.15.4]):
they are how a strategy restricts *how* computation happens, and each is an
observable, specified outcome ([LCSP.2.3], [RTCT.12]). The binding fields
that record the settings themselves ([RBND.1.3]) differ by definition, and are
not output. An engine behaviour that differs between settings in any other
observable is a determinism defect, whatever the setting that selected it.
